P1 - YOURS (swarm-runtime). Advertised verb a default-grant worker cannot perform. swarm-runtime.mjs:4562 pushes 'swarm.check' into availableActions for anyone holding `contribute`; :4583-4584 sets actionTargets['swarm.check'] to contributionTargets, which for a contribute-only caller is exactly [itself]; dispatch then refuses that one target at :8889-8896 (`self_check_refused`, rule check-reviewer-independence) and refuses every other target at :7971-7972 (needs `review`). Net: offered, aimed at itself, impossible both ways. This contradicts the comment at :4560-4565 that the view 'can no more overstate an authority than dispatch can overlook one'. Fix is a one-liner whichever ruling you take: drop the :4562 push, or make the target set empty for contribute-only callers, or admit a contributor to check a DIFFERENT seat's contribution. Mirror rule :4563 (review -> offer capture) is correct and needs nothing.

P1 - YOURS (swarm-native-access / application callback hook). The root-only reviewer/lander fact is a BYPASS, not a check: `_permit` (:2012-2019) refuses only when `member` is truthy, and `_caller` (:2003-2011) returns null for an unscoped principal, refusing only a SCOPED non-member ('swarm_membership_required'). So the deployment owner/root passes every gate - including `organize` (swarm.integrate, :1104) and `review` - with no predicate anywhere naming root. Restriction is asymmetric by construction: members must HOLD the permission, the root holds everything by not being a member. Grants are root-sourced: :8137-8144 refuses delegation beyond the caller's own set and DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS (:1071) carries neither review nor organize. If the objective is to remove a root-only restriction, this pair is the site; if it is to keep one, it is currently implicit and worth naming.

reportTurnEnd retry/wake audit at 9a1a3b48 (chunk 1 of 2), plus the self-leave seam you asked for.

RETRY - THE GUARDS ARE RIGHT, THEIR FOUNDATION IS NOT. Three levels: the durable row keyed swarm-turn-report:<swarmId>:<participantId>:<workerId>:<turnSeq> through priorCoordinationEvent, the ':delivered' marker checked before any send, and the in-flight _turnReportDeliveries map, with the guidance send carrying that same key as its idempotencyKey so a retry replays. Good shape, and 572-c pins the concurrent case.

THE HOLE: the key's uniqueness rests on an UNVALIDATED harness field. swarm.turn_reported is written only at swarm-runtime.mjs:6308 and is validated NOWHERE - not in swarm-state.mjs, not in swarm-event-schemas.mjs. reportTurnEnd validates swarmId and participantId (by lookup) but takes workerId, turnSeq, turnEpoch and report raw from the hook. A hook that omits turnSeq, or repeats it, makes every turn of that seat share ONE key; then priorCoordinationEvent(key) reuses the FIRST report row and the ':delivered' guard returns before delivery - so every later turn is silently swallowed, row and wake both, with no refusal anywhere. That is the failure mode to close before the native callback ships, because the hook is exactly the untrusted caller. Fix: require turnSeq to be a non-negative safe integer and workerId to be the reporting participant's own worker, refusing before the key is built; and put turnEpoch in the key too, since a reincarnated seat may restart turn numbering and would otherwise inherit the predecessor's delivered marker.

RETRY OTHERWISE: the marker is written only when state === 'delivered', so a refused delivery retries on the next call - correct. There is no attempt cap (unbounded retry), which is fine once the wake half exists. But the caller cannot tell delivered from not delivered: reportTurnEnd returns the report event on every path, including the early returns. Return {event, delivery} so the hook can log or retry and so a test can assert the refusal path the way 572-g asserts it f
